findings.where: Screen 7, Independent or not (SHOW text and panel captions)
findings.what: The screen states that only 0u + 0v lands on zero and that 2u + (−4, −2) does, and puts the word independent next to them, but no screen says why a mix that is not all zeros landing on zero means one arrow is a mix of the others, or why real cell area leaves only 0u + 0v. That is the explain's move-it-across argument, and screens 10 and 12 and the closing line all rest on it. Add one sentence each way, for example: if a u + b v = 0 with b not 0, then v = −(a ÷ b) u, on u's line; cells with real area give each point just one mix, so (0, 0) can only be 0u + 0v.

findings.where: Screens 9 and 10, A third arrow and Read the staircase
findings.what: No SHOW screen teaches the elimination test before screen 10 asks him to read a staircase. The test is: put the arrows in as columns and solve a u + b v + c w = 0; all zeros always works, so it is never inconsistent; a free letter means dependent. He learns it only from the answer wording, the hints and Why?. One or two sentences at the end of screen 9, or a line on screen 10's picture, would teach it first.

findings.where: Screen 5, Line them up (worked lines above the grid)
findings.what: Once v reaches (−4, −2), the worked lines say the same thing twice, '2u + 1v = (0, 0)' and '2u + 1v lands on (0, 0)', with 'The span is one line' between them. Drop one.

findings.where: Screen 3, The span (text), and screen 11, A basis (demonstration)
findings.what: 'So the paint covers it all' and 'its paint covers the plane' claim more than the paint shows. The paint stops at amounts of ±5. On screen 11, i and j paint only the square from −5 to 5 for about half a second before the morph, which leaves bare strips at the view's left, right and top edges just as the text says the paint covers the plane. Say 'covers the whole view', and start the paint after i and j turn into u and v, or paint i and j wider.

'Whole amounts land on the corners of the slanted grid. The determinant is each cell's area.' stays on the three 3-D screens (9, 10, 12), where there is no slanted grid and the measure is a box's volume. Drop the caption or make it depend on the screen.

findings.where: Screens 8 and 13, Spot the independent pair and Mixed: a basis (opening state)
findings.what: Both puzzles open on a bare squared grid. Under it, a key lists a cell, the span and a slanted grid, none of which is drawn. The opening looks empty until he picks. Hide the key until a pick, or draw the three choices faintly.

None of the 13 screens shows the three-phase comparison, the lesson's one link to his trade: L1 and L2 at 120° span the plane, and L1 + L2 + L3 = 0, so the three are dependent. A steps lesson shows only the frame, so he meets it only in the dossier. One sentence on screen 7 or 11 would bring it into the lesson.

No screen says where these words go next, such as lesson 2's change of basis and lesson 6's eigenbasis, though the brief lists this as where the lesson is used. A closing half-sentence on screen 11 would do.

The description has 'A 3-D switch adds a third part' and says to drag either arrow's tip as if that works on every screen. The build has no switch: the 3-D view is its own three screens, and tips drag only on screens 3 and 5.

'This matters for the two masses on springs' names lesson 7's example as if he already knew it, and 'every shudder' is vague. 'You divide by its amount' should say to pick an arrow whose amount is not 0.
